taxonomy_note: Older Flora of North America treatment places Celtis in Ulmaceae; current Kew/POWO places Celtis in Cannabaceae. The learner follows current Cannabaceae placement while retaining older source context.
where_to_look_first: Start with the leaf base and venation, then confirm with fruit. Hackberries (Celtis) often have a strongly 3-nerved/asymmetric leaf base and make fleshy drupes; elms (Ulmus) have pinnate venation and make flat winged samaras.

cues: Many Celtis leaves are 3-nerved from near the base, though exact venation varies by species.
Surface may feel scabrous due to cystoliths.
Fruit is a fleshy drupe with one hard stone.
Some local Celtis species may be thorny/spinescent.
Venation is pinnate; secondary veins run toward the serrated margin and often terminate at teeth.
Margins commonly serrate to doubly serrate.
Fruit is a flattened membranous winged samara.
Some species/twigs may develop corky wings.
Ulmaceae_Ulmus.strongest_confirmation: Flat winged samara + pinnate serrated elm leaf.

local_priority_cards.look_here_first: Smooth/light-gray often corky-warty bark plus mostly entire to sparsely toothed narrow leaves; confirm with orange/red/brown drupes.
confirm: Margins mostly entire or only sparsely toothed.
Fruit a nearly round fleshy drupe.

local_priority_cards.look_here_first: Strongly netted/reticulate leaf venation on a small hackberry leaf; confirm with fleshy drupe.
local_priority_cards.note: Canonical learner should use Celtis reticulata; Celtis laevigata var. reticulata is retained only as a historical/source synonym row.

local_priority_cards.look_here_first: Small rough cedar-elm leaf with an oblique base and serrate-to-doubly-serrate margin; confirm with samara fruit.
confirm: Leaves are usually under about 7 cm in the FNA vegetative key.
Upper leaf surface is harshly pubescent/scabrous.
Fruit is a flat winged samara.

visual_targets: Celtis leaf showing asymmetric base and 3 basal veins
Ulmus crassifolia rough leaf with oblique base and double serration
side-by-side Celtis drupe vs Ulmus samara
learner_rule: If the leaves look vaguely elm-like, do not stop at the leaf. Fruit type is the fastest family-level tie breaker.
